children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he is currently in approved education or training.

Could you tell me if Alex is currently in full-time, non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar) or approved training? Or has he finished his education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's finished his education. He's not studying anything at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

Since Alex has finished his education, I have a couple more questions:

Is Alex currently registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services? (If so, and if he's registered within the last 20 weeks, you may still be eligible for Child Benefit during that period.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with anything like that. He just finished school and is at home now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying.

I have one more question to complete my assessment:

Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working that much - he doesn't have a job at the moment. And he's not receiving any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information.

Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to make an eligibility assessment for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

- **Age and education:** Child Benefit normally applies to children under 16. For children aged 16-19, eligibility can continue only if they remain in **approved education or training** (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications).

- **Alex's situation:** Since Alex is 18 and has finished his education and is not in any approved training, he no longer meets the criteria for Child Benefit.

- **Registration option:** There is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a **16 or 17 year old** registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services after leaving education. Unfortunately, this option only applies to 16 and 17 year olds, and Alex is 18.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. If Alex decides to return to approved education or training before he turns 20, you may become eligible again at that point. If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask.

reasonings: Alex is 18 years old and has finished his education. For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit can only continue if the child stays in approved education or training. Since Alex is no longer in approved education or training, this route to eligibility does not apply. Additionally, Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services - however, Alex is 18 and has not registered with either of these services. Although Alex is not working 24+ hours per week and is not receiving benefits in his own name (which would have ended eligibility), he still does not meet the criteria because he is over 16 and not in approved education or training. Therefore, there is no qualifying basis for Child Benefit for Alex.
